comparisons.peer_topic: DRAM production nodes and future expectations
comparisons.peer_summary: The company shipped its industry's first 1β production node in 2023, produced majority 2024 bits on 1α and 1β nodes, and expects volume shipments of the 1γ node using EUV lithography in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron describe ongoing process technology development involving significant capital investment in advanced lithography to improve performance, power efficiency, and cost. Intel explicitly cites EUV lithography as part of its ongoing investment for improving existing designs and developing new nodes like Intel 18A and 14A. Micron similarly reports on its DRAM node progress, noting that its next-generation 1γ node will employ EUV lithography for volume shipments, highlighting a shared reliance on this specific manufacturing technology for leading-edge nodes.

sentences.text: The continued development of leading-edge nodes that are competitive with the offerings of other foundries requires significant ongoing capital investment as we pursue incremental improvements and refinements of existing transistor and layout designs and manufacturing technologies, such as EUV lithography, while also pursuing new transistor and layout designs, such as gate-all-around and backside power in our upcoming Intel 18A process node, and new manufacturing technologies, such as high-NA EUV lithography for use in our upcoming Intel 14A process node.
In 2023, we began shipping the industry's first 1β (1-beta) production node, which offers further improvements in power efficiency and bit density.
We expect volume shipments in 2025 of our next generation of DRAM, the 1γ (1-gamma) node, which will employ EUV lithography production.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company is on track for volume production of 1-gamma DRAM using EUV lithography in calendar 2025 and has begun volume production of its Micron G9 NAND node.
comparisons.comparison: Similar to the comparison above, Micron's disclosure confirms volume production plans for a node using EUV lithography, directly paralleling Intel's stated requirement for 'significant ongoing capital investment' in EUV lithography to maintain competitive process nodes. Intel focuses on gate-all-around and backside power alongside EUV for upcoming nodes, while Micron focuses on the transition to EUV for its 1-gamma DRAM node, showing a common industry driver in adopting EUV for next-generation manufacturing efficiency.

sentences.text: The continued development of leading-edge nodes that are competitive with the offerings of other foundries requires significant ongoing capital investment as we pursue incremental improvements and refinements of existing transistor and layout designs and manufacturing technologies, such as EUV lithography, while also pursuing new transistor and layout designs, such as gate-all-around and backside power in our upcoming Intel 18A process node, and new manufacturing technologies, such as high-NA EUV lithography for use in our upcoming Intel 14A process node.
Our 1-gamma DRAM pilot production using EUV lithography is progressing well, and we are on track for volume production in calendar 2025.
